title: Prostate Cancer Survivorship: Community PSA Monitoring and Side-Effect Management

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult man in a Saudi primary health centre or community clinic who has returned to primary care after curative-intent treatment for prostate cancer (radical prostatectomy, radiotherapy, brachytherapy or related treatment): visit and PSA schedule, how to recognise biochemical recurrence and when to send him back to the treating urologist or oncologist, and how to manage late effects (sexual, urinary, bowel, hot flushes, bone health, mood). Uses the 2020 British Columbia primary-care follow-up guideline adapted from Cancer Care Ontario, a Saudi Cancer Registry review and Saudi PSA reference data, with product labels. Not for initial diagnosis, active surveillance, castration-resistant or metastatic disease, or palliative care.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Health Council primary-care follow-up guideline for prostate cancer survivors was found. A Saudi national prostate cancer guideline hosted on the Saudi Health Council website appeared in search results but the document could not be opened (the link returned a page-not-found error), so its follow-up recommendations were not read. The schedule below is Canadian and its evidence is mostly expert consensus.

The British Columbia guideline states it is based on scientific evidence current to November 2017 and adapted from Cancer Care Ontario clinical guidance; newer studies and any later update were not checked.

PSA intervals are explicitly described by the guideline as based on working-group consensus, not trial evidence; the guideline says surveillance intensity should reflect risk of recurrence and clinical judgement should be used.

PSA values in the guideline are in micrograms per litre (equal to ng/mL). The thresholds for relapse after radical prostatectomy (two successive rises to above 0.2) and after radiotherapy (nadir plus 2) are definitions from the guideline's Table 2 and were not checked against a Saudi centre's protocol.

Saudi PSA reference ranges (a 2019 study of 7,814 Saudi men with 95th percentile 3.8 ng/mL at ages 60 to 70) apply to men without prostate cancer and must not be used to judge recurrence after treatment; only the abstract of that study was read.

The Saudi Cancer Registry review (3,607 patients, 2008 to 2017) gives epidemiology and stage at diagnosis (60.4% localized; 31.4% metastasis rate) but no survivorship or side-effect data; Saudi data on late effects, erectile dysfunction rates and access to penile rehabilitation or continence physiotherapy were not found.

Calcium and vitamin D supplementation and bone density testing are advised for men on androgen deprivation therapy, but the guideline gives no dose; no calcium or vitamin D regimen is written. Bisphosphonates, denosumab and the osteoporosis guideline it refers to were not read.

The guideline lists estradiol, cyproterone acetate, megestrol acetate and medroxyprogesterone for hot flushes as off-label options with serious adverse effects; only venlafaxine was checked against a label and the others are not written as regimens. The dose of venlafaxine for hot flushes comes from the guideline (initial 37.5 mg daily, usual 37.5 to 150 mg, maximum 225 mg) and is not a labelled indication.

Tamsulosin is labelled for benign prostatic hyperplasia, and solifenacin for overactive bladder; use after prostate cancer treatment follows the guideline and is outside the label indication for tamsulosin.

Loperamide: the guideline lists 4 mg after the first loose stool then 2 mg after each loose stool to a maximum of 16 mg a day; the United States over-the-counter label allows no more than 4 softgels (8 mg) in 24 hours. Use the label limit unless a specialist directs otherwise; this must be reconciled locally.

Testosterone therapy, androgen deprivation therapy itself, salvage treatment, penile rehabilitation devices, injection and implant therapy and radiation proctitis treatments are for specialists and are not written as regimens.
Figures were read by automated extraction of the guideline PDF, article and label text; spot-check each value and dose against the source during clinical review.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: After curative treatment, a rise in PSA signals possible recurrence long before symptoms; a recurrence is detected at a much lower PSA than the laboratory's 'abnormal' flag, for example above 0.2 µg/L after radical prostatectomy (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Key Recommendations). After radiotherapy PSA falls to a lowest value (nadir) and relapse is defined as nadir plus 2; after brachytherapy PSA may 'bounce' to 4 µg/L or more for 1 to 3 years without recurrence (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 2). Long-lasting effects usually occur more than three months after surgery or radiation, or during or after androgen deprivation therapy: sexual, urinary and bowel dysfunction, anaemia, body composition change, fatigue, hot flushes, bone loss and psychological distress (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 3). In Saudi Arabia prostate cancer is usually found late in the elderly: mean age at diagnosis 71.1 years, 60.4% localized and 31.4% with metastasis in the registry review (Saudi Cancer Registry review, Section Abstract). Quality of life and satisfaction are higher in survivors who have access to survivorship care (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Survivorship).

symptoms: Severe and progressive bone pain, blood in the urine, new urinary symptoms (urgency, voiding discomfort, nocturia, obstruction) or significant incontinence needing pads (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).
New bowel symptoms: rectal bleeding, rectal pain, urgency or change in bowel habit (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).
Fatigue and unexplained weight loss (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).
Erectile dysfunction, loss of libido, dry ejaculate, hot flushes and breast tenderness (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 3).
Low mood, anxiety and fear of recurrence (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 3).
physicalSigns: Routine digital rectal examination is not required after treatment of localized disease unless PSA recurrence or symptoms need evaluating (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).
Pallor or low haemoglobin on androgen deprivation therapy (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).
Gynaecomastia or breast tenderness in men on androgen deprivation therapy (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 3).
redFlags: Any measurable PSA rise after radical prostatectomy, two successive rises to above 0.2 µg/L, or nadir plus 2 after radiotherapy: refer back to the treating urologist or radiation oncologist (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 2).
Severe and progressive bone pain, or new constitutional symptoms with weight loss: check PSA and consider referral back to the specialist (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).
Haematuria: refer to a urologist (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

Rectal bleeding in any man, including after radiotherapy: refer for colonoscopy; do not biopsy the anterior rectum because of the risk of fistula (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

Persistent urinary leakage affecting quality of life, or incontinence more than a year after prostatectomy: refer to a urologist; sling or artificial sphincter may be considered (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
Erectile dysfunction not responding to a phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor: refer to a urologist or sexual health expert (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
Psychological distress on screening: offer therapy or medicine and refer to specialised care or a support group (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
precipitants: Radical prostatectomy: infertility, erectile dysfunction, urinary incontinence and obstructive urinary symptoms (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 3 and Section Appendix B).
Radiotherapy: urinary and bowel dysfunction including rectal bleeding, urgency and frequency (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 3).
Androgen deprivation therapy: anaemia, hot flushes, bone loss, gynaecomastia, fatigue and body composition change (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 3).
Older age at diagnosis (mean age 71.1 years in Saudi Arabia) raises fracture, frailty and cardiovascular concerns (Saudi Cancer Registry review, Section Abstract).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Two successive PSA rises above 0.2 µg/L after prostatectomy, or nadir plus 2 after radiotherapy (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 2).
Temporary rise, possibly to 4 µg/L or more, for 1 to 3 years without recurrence (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 2).
Rectal bleeding after pelvic radiotherapy; still needs colonoscopy and specialist input (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

differentials.condition: Bladder neck contracture or urethral stricture
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Obstructive symptoms after prostatectomy; refer to urology (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
Persistent low mood or worry; screen with the Patient Health Questionnaire (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

clinicalManagement.title: Receive the man back from the treating team
actions: Obtain the treatment summary: type of treatment, date, pathology, last PSA and nadir, androgen deprivation therapy and the follow-up plan (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Scope).
Agree who owns PSA review and when to send him back to the urologist or radiation oncologist (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Key Recommendations).

clinicalManagement.title: Set the visit and PSA schedule
actions: See the man after 3 months, then every 6 months in year 1, every 6 months in year 2 and every 12 months in year 3 (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).

PSA after surgery: every 3 months in year 1, every 6 months in years 2 and 3, then annually; after radiotherapy: every 6 months in years 1 and 2, every 12 months in year 3 (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).
Review the exact PSA value and the trend; do not rely on the laboratory's abnormal flag (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Key Recommendations).
No routine digital rectal examination (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).

clinicalManagement.title: Detect and act on recurrence
actions: Refer back to the treating physician for two successive rises above 0.2 µg/L after prostatectomy or nadir plus 2 after radiotherapy or brachytherapy (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 2).
Do not mistake a post-brachytherapy PSA bounce for recurrence; discuss with the specialist (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 2).
Do PSA and consider referral for severe bone pain, haematuria, new urinary or bowel symptoms or weight loss (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).

clinicalManagement.title: Protect bone and blood in men on androgen deprivation therapy
actions: Arrange baseline dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry and FRAX, and recommend calcium and vitamin D (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).
Check a full blood count yearly and investigate any anaemia (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Table 1).
Encourage exercise to limit fatigue and body composition change (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat sexual dysfunction
actions: Offer a phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor first (see medicines); refer to a urologist or sexual health expert if it fails (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

Refer men and partners for sexual health counselling for loss of libido or anorgasmia; explain dry ejaculate; teach emptying the bladder, condom use, penile constriction band and Kegel exercises for climacturia (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
Tell men and partners that radical prostatectomy causes infertility, while some men after radiotherapy remain fertile (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
Testosterone therapy only by the treating oncologist or urologist in documented deficiency with no evidence of recurrence (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat urinary and bowel symptoms
actions: Obstructive symptoms: alpha-blocker if no radical prostatectomy; refer men to urology for possible bladder neck contracture or urethral stricture (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
Urgency: antimuscarinic or beta-3 agonist if post-void residual is under 200 mL; refractory symptoms to urology (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

Incontinence: pelvic floor exercises with physiotherapist or continence nurse; refer persistent leakage and any incontinence beyond a year after prostatectomy (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

Bowel urgency or frequency after radiotherapy: bulking diet, hydration, antidiarrhoeal and pelvic floor therapy; refer rectal bleeding for colonoscopy (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat hot flushes and mood
actions: For troublesome hot flushes on androgen deprivation therapy consider an off-label option such as venlafaxine, weighing harms (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
Screen mood with the Patient Health Questionnaire; offer therapy or medicine and a support group (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).

Consider the survivorship programme and advance care planning when disease is advanced (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Sections Survivorship and Palliative Care and Advance Care Planning).

regimens.indication: Erectile dysfunction after prostate cancer treatment
regimens.patientGroup: Adult men with erectile dysfunction after prostate cancer treatment
regimens.dose: 50 mg taken as needed about 1 hour before sexual activity (may be taken 30 minutes to 4 hours before); the dose may be increased to 100 mg or reduced to 25 mg by effect and tolerance (Viagra label, Section 2.1; BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix C). Dilution and preparation: none; swallow the tablet whole.
regimens.route: Oral, with or without food (Viagra label, Section 2.2)
regimens.frequency: As needed; no more than once a day (Viagra label, Section 2.1)
regimens.duration: Long-term as needed; review effect and tolerance at each follow-up visit
adjustments: Start at 25 mg if aged over 65, with hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance under 30 mL/min), or taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or erythromycin (Viagra label, Sections 2.4 and 2.5).
Ritonavir: 25 mg, maximum 25 mg in 48 hours (Viagra label, Section 2.4).
With an alpha-blocker, be stable on the alpha-blocker first and start at 25 mg (Viagra label, Section 2.3).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Blood pressure and dizziness, particularly with alpha-blockers or antihypertensives (Viagra label, Section 5.5).
Erection lasting more than 4 hours: emergency (Viagra label, Section 5.2).
Sudden vision or hearing loss: stop and seek help (Viagra label, Sections 5.3 and 5.4).
contraindications: Any form of organic nitrate, regular or intermittent (Viagra label, Section 4.1).
Known hypersensitivity to sildenafil (Viagra label, Section 4.2).
Guanylate cyclase stimulator such as riociguat (Viagra label, Section 4.3).
regimens.branch: Erectile dysfunction after prostate cancer treatment
regimens.useWhen: As-needed use is the usual first choice

regimens.indication: Erectile dysfunction after prostate cancer treatment
regimens.patientGroup: Adult men with erectile dysfunction after prostate cancer treatment
regimens.dose: As needed: 10 mg before anticipated sexual activity, adjusted to 20 mg or 5 mg; or once daily: 2.5 mg at about the same time each day, increased to 5 mg (Cialis label, Sections 2.1 and 2.2; BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix C). Do not split tablets. Dilution and preparation: none.
regimens.route: Oral, without regard to food (Cialis label, Section 2.5)
regimens.frequency: As needed no more than once a day, or once daily at the same time
regimens.duration: Long-term; review effect and tolerance at each follow-up visit
adjustments: Renal impairment, creatinine clearance 30 to 50 mL/min: as-needed start at 5 mg, maximum 10 mg once every 48 hours; under 30 mL/min: maximum 5 mg once every 72 hours; once-daily use not recommended (Cialis label, Section 2.6).
Mild or moderate hepatic impairment: do not exceed 10 mg once a day; severe: not recommended (Cialis label, Section 2.6).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Blood pressure with alpha-blockers and antihypertensives (Cialis label, Section 5.6); back pain and myalgia (Cialis label, Section 6).
Priapism, sudden vision or hearing loss: stop and seek help (Cialis label, Sections 5.3 to 5.5).
contraindications: Any form of organic nitrate (Cialis label, Section 4.1).
Known serious hypersensitivity to tadalafil (Cialis label, Section 4.2).
Guanylate cyclase stimulator such as riociguat (Cialis label, Section 4.3).
regimens.branch: Erectile dysfunction after prostate cancer treatment
regimens.useWhen: Once-daily dosing, or a longer window of effect

regimens.indication: Obstructive urinary symptoms after prostate cancer treatment (off-label use)
regimens.patientGroup: Men who have not had radical prostatectomy
regimens.dose: 0.4 mg once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day; if no response after 2 to 4 weeks the label allows 0.8 mg once daily (Flomax label, Section 2; BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix C). Dilution and preparation: none; swallow the capsule whole, do not crush, chew or open.
regimens.frequency: Once daily; restart at 0.4 mg if stopped for several days (Flomax label, Section 2)
adjustments: Do not use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole; use caution with moderate inhibitors and with cimetidine (Flomax label, Section 5.2).
Do not use with other alpha-adrenergic blockers (Flomax label, Section 5.2).
Not for men after radical prostatectomy (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
Cataract or glaucoma surgery: intraoperative floppy iris syndrome; do not start in a man scheduled for such surgery (Flomax label, Section 5.5).
Sulfa allergy: caution (Flomax label, Section 5.6).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Orthostatic hypotension, dizziness and syncope, especially after the first dose (Flomax label, Section 5.1).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to tamsulosin or any component (Flomax label, Section 4).

regimens.dose: 5 mg once daily; if well tolerated the dose may be increased to 10 mg once daily (Solifenacin label, Section 2.1; BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix C). Dilution and preparation: none; swallow whole with water.
regimens.route: Oral, with or without food (Solifenacin label, Section 2.1)
regimens.duration: Review after a trial period; stop if no benefit or if retention develops
adjustments: Severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance under 30 mL/min): do not exceed 5 mg daily (Solifenacin label, Section 2.2).
Moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B): do not exceed 5 mg daily; severe: do not use (Solifenacin label, Section 2.3).
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole: do not exceed 5 mg daily (Solifenacin label, Section 2.4).

monitoring: Post-void residual before starting and if symptoms change; stop if retention develops (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
Dry mouth and constipation (Solifenacin label, Section 6).
QT prolongation in men at high risk (Solifenacin label, Section 5.6).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to solifenacin or its excipients (Solifenacin label, Section 4).

regimens.indication: Bowel urgency and frequency after pelvic radiotherapy
regimens.patientGroup: Adults with loose stools after radiotherapy and no blood in the stool
regimens.dose: 2 capsules (4 mg) after the first loose stool, then 1 capsule (2 mg) after each loose stool; no more than 4 capsules (8 mg) in 24 hours on the over-the-counter label (Imodium A-D label, Directions; BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix C lists a maximum of 16 mg a day under medical supervision). Dilution and preparation: none; drink plenty of clear fluids.
regimens.duration: Short courses; stop and ask a doctor if diarrhoea lasts more than 2 days (Imodium A-D label, Stop use and ask a doctor)
adjustments: Liver disease or abnormal heart rhythm: ask a doctor before use (Imodium A-D label, Ask a doctor).

Pregnancy or breast-feeding: ask a health professional (Imodium A-D label).

monitoring: Taking more than directed can cause serious heart problems or death (Imodium A-D label, Heart alert).
Abdominal swelling, worsening symptoms, fever or mucus: stop and review (Imodium A-D label).
contraindications: Allergy to loperamide (Imodium A-D label, Allergy alert).
Bloody or black stool (Imodium A-D label, Do not use).
Children under 12 years (Imodium A-D label, Do not use).

regimens.indication: Hot flushes during androgen deprivation therapy (off-label use)
regimens.patientGroup: Men on androgen deprivation therapy with troublesome hot flushes
regimens.dose: Start 37.5 mg once daily; usual 37.5 to 150 mg once daily; maximum 225 mg a day (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix C). Dilution and preparation: none; swallow the capsule whole, or open it and sprinkle the contents on a spoonful of applesauce and swallow immediately without chewing, followed by water (Venlafaxine label, Section 2.1).
regimens.route: Oral, once daily with food, morning or evening at about the same time (Venlafaxine label, Section 2.1)
regimens.duration: Review benefit and adverse effects; do not stop abruptly: taper (Venlafaxine label, Section 2.10)
adjustments: Hepatic impairment: reduce the total daily dose by 50% (mild to moderate) or more (severe) (Venlafaxine label, Section 2.8).
Renal impairment: reduce the dose by 25% to 50% (mild to moderate) or 50% or more (severe or dialysis) (Venlafaxine label, Section 2.9).
At least 14 days between stopping a monoamine oxidase inhibitor and starting venlafaxine, and 7 days after stopping venlafaxine before an MAOI (Venlafaxine label, Section 2.11).
Off-label for hot flushes; use with caution (BC Guidelines prostate cancer follow-up 2020, Section Appendix B).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Blood pressure, since the drug causes dose-related hypertension (Venlafaxine label, Section 5.3).
Mood and suicidal thoughts, particularly early in treatment (Venlafaxine label, Section 5.1).
Serotonin syndrome, bleeding risk, hyponatraemia and sexual dysfunction (Venlafaxine label, Sections 5.2, 5.4, 5.9 and 5.13).
Discontinuation symptoms on missed doses or stopping (Venlafaxine label, Section 5.7).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine or excipients (Venlafaxine label, Section 4).
Taking or within 14 days of stopping a monoamine oxidase inhibitor, including linezolid and intravenous methylene blue (Venlafaxine label, Section 4).

branches.label: Urgency symptoms with complete bladder emptying
branches.entryCriteria: Man with urgency who empties the bladder completely (post-void residual under 200 mL), with no urinary retention, gastric retention or uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma.

branches.label: Bowel urgency and frequency after radiotherapy
branches.entryCriteria: Man with bowel urgency or frequency after pelvic radiotherapy, with no blood in the stool, fever or mucus.

branches.label: Hot flushes during androgen deprivation therapy
branches.entryCriteria: Man on androgen deprivation therapy with troublesome hot flushes not controlled by non-drug measures, not taking a monoamine oxidase inhibitor.

medicationPlan.note: Six medicines are written for late effects of prostate cancer treatment, taken from the guideline's list for primary care. The guideline names each medicine and adult dose; the dilution (none for oral forms), administration, adjustments and contraindications come from the product labels. Hot-flush use of venlafaxine and obstructive-symptom use of tamsulosin are outside the labelled indication. All doses are for adults. SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

teaching.scope: Adult man in a Saudi primary health centre or community clinic who has returned to primary care after curative-intent treatment for prostate cancer (radical prostatectomy, radiotherapy, brachytherapy or related treatment): visit and PSA schedule, how to recognise biochemical recurrence and when to send him back to the treating urologist or oncologist, and how to manage late effects (sexual, urinary, bowel, hot flushes, bone health, mood). Uses the 2020 British Columbia primary-care follow-up guideline adapted from Cancer Care Ontario, a Saudi Cancer Registry review and Saudi PSA reference data, with product labels. Not for initial diagnosis, active surveillance, castration-resistant or metastatic disease, or palliative care.
learningObjectives: Follow the visit and PSA schedule after curative treatment.
Know the PSA definition of recurrence for surgery and for radiotherapy.
Treat late effects with first-line medicines and refer when they fail.
Protect bone and blood in men on androgen deprivation therapy.
pitfalls: Using Saudi untreated-man PSA ranges to judge recurrence.
Missing nitrate use before a phosphodiesterase inhibitor.
Starting an antimuscarinic without checking bladder emptying.
Skipping bone assessment on androgen deprivation therapy.
keyPoints: Laboratory 'normal' flags miss recurrence after prostatectomy.
A PSA bounce after brachytherapy is not always recurrence.
Rectal bleeding after radiotherapy still needs colonoscopy.
Tamsulosin is not for men after radical prostatectomy.

patientEducation: After treatment you will have regular check-ups and blood tests for PSA; a rise can be an early sign that the cancer is coming back, so every result matters.
Erections, bladder and bowel control can change after treatment; effective treatments are available, so please tell your doctor.
Never take a tablet for erections if you use nitrate medicines for the heart.
Go to hospital at once if an erection lasts more than 4 hours.
Tell us about low mood or worry; support is available for you and your partner.
lifestyleAndDiet: Join a support group if available.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician; urologist; radiation or medical oncologist; continence nurse or pelvic-floor physiotherapist; sexual health counsellor; dietitian; psychologist or psychiatrist; palliative care team if disease advances.
dischargeCriteria: Treatment summary and last PSA recorded; PSA and visit schedule given; relapse criteria and who to call; list of medicines for late effects with contraindications; warning symptoms (bone pain, blood in urine or stool, prolonged erection).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: PSA and review visits per the schedule (surgery: 3-monthly in year 1; radiotherapy: 6-monthly), annual full blood count and bone review on androgen deprivation therapy, and refer back to the treating specialist on any biochemical relapse.
